gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured recording size for any sub-$50 camera: Vortex Radar measured the 70mai M310 at about 92 MB per minute at 1296p30 (roughly 5.5 GB an hour, so about 46 hours on its 256 GB maximum card), and no named reviewer or lab has published a measurement for the DDPAI N2 or Mini models that ChatGPT also recommends.
standout_why: Compared against Auto Roamer (cited), GuideSpot (cited), the DashCamTalk price tracker (cited) and DashCamTalk's best-of page. Auto Roamer has no measured figures at all (it says its picks come from maker specs, owner reports and third-party reviews). GuideSpot's only M310 test figure is the author's 'voice control responds about 70% of the time' over 30 days, with no file size, bitrate, heat or power figure. The DashCamTalk tracker gives price and a 6.3 rating for the M310 but no sub-scores or measurements on that page. Dash & Drive (cited) could not be opened (certificate error on fetch; curl and the Web Archive were blocked), so it is unchecked and the score is held at 2 for that reason. No page opened gives any named measurement for a DDPAI under-$50 model.
decides: It confirms the 70mai M310 line as the pick on named evidence rather than changing it: it is the only sub-$50 family with scores and a measurement from named sources. DashCamTalk scores the M310 Plus 4K 6.8 against the M310's 6.3 at almost the same Amazon price on 2026-11-21 ($39.89 vs $39.99), with identical 7/10 day and 5/10 night video scores; the gap comes from reliability (6 vs 5) and support (6 vs 4), plus buffered parking mode. So the named scores point to the Plus 4K over the plain M310 that ChatGPT picked. Both use an internal battery, which DashCamTalk and Vortex Radar flag for hot weather. The DDPAI N2 Front (a partner product, $49.00 before code per the brief's table) can only win the supercapacitor/hot-climate segment on the maker's own spec; no named test backs it, and the page should say so. Our five linked dash cams are all $157 and up through our link, so none fits the budget on the question's own terms.

findings.label: Recording file size, measured by Vortex Radar
findings.value: about 92 MB per minute at 1296p 30 fps
findings.source_title: 70mai M310 Review (Vortex Radar, DashCamTalk forum, posted 2026-02-17)
findings.note: Quote: "file sizes are small at only ~92 MB/min". Our arithmetic, not the reviewer's: 92 MB × 60 = 5.52 GB per hour; a 32 GB card holds about 5.8 hours, 64 GB about 11.6 hours, the 256 GB maximum about 46 hours before loop overwrite (decimal GB, ignoring formatting overhead); 92 MB/min × 8 ÷ 60 ≈ 12.3 Mbps average. Reviewer bought a pair of M310 units; firmware version not stated.

findings.label: Parking and mode-switch timing, observed by Vortex Radar
findings.value: about 2 seconds to switch from time-lapse to normal recording; hardwired non-buffered collision detection starts recording "essentially instantly (not 1-2 sec)"
findings.source_title: 70mai M310 Review (Vortex Radar, DashCamTalk forum, posted 2026-02-17)
findings.note: Needs the hardwire kit. Same post: Wi-Fi transfers are "pretty slow since it only uses 2.4 GHz" (no number given) and it has an "internal battery unfortunately instead of a supercapacitor, so there's the usual fire risk in hot weather" (a judgement, no temperature measured).
